subject: Conflicting slot labels on Chili Piper — localized time shows differently
body:
From: Amina Rahman <amina@novacorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Scheduling the Redwood demo (slot shows different local time)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. I tried booking via the Chili Piper link you sent, but the time slot labelled "10:00 AM" appears as 9:00 AM on my calendar after I confirm — NovaCorp is in London and we're currently on GMT (no DST this week). I'm worried we'll end up misaligned for the live demo.

Can you share an ICS or confirm the UTC offset so I can be sure? Happy to do 10:00 UK time if that's what you intended.

Best,
Amina Rahman
Senior PM, NovaCorp

----
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rahman <amina@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Scheduling the Redwood demo (slot shows different local time)

Hi Amina — thanks for flagging this. Really sorry for the friction. We see two things happen often with Chili Piper and localized slot labels:

- The booking page shows a human-friendly local label ("10:00"), but the follow-up confirmation sometimes writes the event in the calendar using a server-side timezone or a numeric UTC offset that the recipient calendar mis-parses.
- A subset of users in regions with unusual DST transitions (or where their calendar client has its time zone set to "(GMT) London" vs "Europe/London") end up with a one-hour shift.

Workaround options to avoid this:
1) Manually add the UTC offset in the subject when we send the invite (e.g., "Demo — 10:00 GMT / 09:00 UTC+0").
2) I can send an explicit .ics that pins the TZ as Europe/London (I attached one below). Importing that into Google/Outlook preserves the intended local time.
3) Use the alternate booking link that includes the tz query param (I generated a Europe/London version and included it below).

If you confirm "10:00 UK time (Europe/London)", I'll lock in the slot and email the deck + ICS.

Notes for internal folks: Marissa — we should add a short line to the booking page copy recommending "choose your timezone in the drop‑down" and include UTC offset in the confirmation email. Ben — can you check the Chili Piper integration for whether we can force insertion of the TZ identifier (e.g., Europe/London) into the outgoing ICS?

Amina — apologies again. If you prefer, I can book a 10:00 slot manually and email you the calendar item.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 14:45:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: Scheduling the Redwood demo — recurring localized label mismatch

Ben / Integrations team — forwarding an example where Chili Piper created a slot label ("10:00") but the resulting calendar item landed an hour off for the prospect. See Amina's note below.

Ask: can we make the booking confirmation include the explicit TZ name (Europe/London / America/Los_Angeles / Asia/Tokyo) and the numeric UTC offset in parentheses? If Chili Piper can't be configured, can we intercept the webhook and rewrite the ICS with the VTIMEZONE block?

Thanks — Marissa

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scheduling the Redwood demo — recurring localized label mismatch

Thanks for the ping. I dug into the Chili Piper webhook payload for the booking in question. It looks like Chili Piper is shipping an RFC5545 ICS with dates in UTC but without an explicit VTIMEZONE block — some calendar clients then display the event relative to their local TZ inference, which can produce a one-hour discrepancy around DST boundary days.

Short term fix (today): we can intercept the webhook and re-generate the ICS with a VTIMEZONE (Europe/London) and include an explicit DESCRIPTION line with the UTC offset. I'll patch the integrations lambda and generate a one-off ICS for Amina.

Longer term: I'll add a feature request to the integrations backlog to append the TZ identifier to the confirmation subject and to surface a "View in your timezone" helper on the booking page.

-Ben
